source.title: Don't Cut Corners: Exact Conditions for Modularity in Biologically Inspired Representations
source.authors: Will Dorrell; Kyle Hsu; Luke Hollingsworth; Jin Hwa Lee; Jia-Jun Wu; Chelsea Finn; Peter E. Latham; T. Behrens; James C. R. Whittington

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether mixed-selective representations can arise under mechanisms other than the superposition account, using range-dependent source distributions and biologically constrained network models rather than the original toy-superposition setup.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test feature superposition, capacity pressure, LLM activations, or SAEs. Rows cover its own trained-network results on modular versus mixed-selective representations relevant to V3. Cited neuroscience and prior-study results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own trained networks all have more hidden units than sources (e.g. 25 hidden vs 2 sources; 6 latents vs 3 sources; 12 vs 6; 16 RNN units). Mixed-selective (polysemantic) neurons still arise when the sources' joint range is non-rectangular, as in corner cutting or harmonic frequencies. These are direct results on V3: polysemanticity without capacity pressure. The study does not address superposition geometry, SAEs or LLMs.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that range independence (presence of extremal corners), not statistical independence, determines whether nonnegative, energy-efficient networks modularise. They also argue that energy efficiency and omitted variables offer alternative origins of mixed selectivity besides nonlinear classification. They additionally apply this to explain conflicting grid-cell/reward findings.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops and empirically tests a theory of modularisation under nonnegativity and energy constraints, using source-support manipulations in autoencoders and recurrent networks. It does not use the original toy-superposition method or measure feature overlap in an overcomplete sparse-feature model.
record.method_sensitivity: The outcome changes with source-support geometry, corner removal, frequency relationships, and whether a correlated encoded variable is included in the analysis. Correlations that preserve range independence generally affect modularity less than corner cutting.
record.problems: The experiments are synthetic or task-trained network studies rather than LLM or SAE investigations, and they do not directly test superposition. The authors note that the main theory assumes perfect reconstruction and focuses on one-dimensional sources; the nonlinear extensions are empirical and are reported mainly as qualitative trends. Several plotted results are described without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. Results about prior neuroscience studies and other cited work were excluded because they are not results produced by this study.

untested.parts: No language models or SAEs are tested. The study does not show that superposition is absent in its networks beyond the dz>ds setup. The mechanism is tied to nonnegativity plus energy (activity/weight) regularisation.
Not tested: no sparse-feature, overcomplete toy model, no sparsity transition, no geometry.
Not tested directly. The study gives an alternative non-capacity route to mixing but does not measure capacity competition or feature importance.
Not tested. Multi-dimensional sources appear only in a theoretical sufficiency extension (Appendix B.5).

missing.what: Without biological constraints (no ReLU or energy regularisation), What-Where networks are mixed-selective even with independent sources. This is another non-capacity route to polysemanticity.
Imperfect reconstruction: with range-independent four-point data, lowering the reconstruction penalty makes the representation mix.
Across many generated datasets, the paper's inequality violation predicts the mixing angle, whereas source multiinformation does not.

record.verdict_notes: I dropped the reader's limits_scope label. V3 is an existence claim (polysemanticity 'can' arise for other reasons), so modular controls do not qualify it; they act as controls for the mechanism. The 'no capacity pressure' reading rests on dz>ds in every reported setting (Theorem 2.1 assumes dz>ds; architectures in Appendices F-H). The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition only in related work and does not frame its results as being about superposition.

versions.untested_parts: The paper studies modular versus mixed-selective representations, not sparse-feature superposition, its sparsity-dependent transition, or superposition geometry.
It does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by limited feature capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
No LLMs or other language models are tested, and the paper does not directly measure whether mixed-selective units imply or fail to imply superposition.
No LLM feature-spreading or SAE-recovery experiments are reported.
The paper does not assess whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Although the theory focuses on one-dimensional sources and discusses a multidimensional extension, it does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions.

rows.subject: optimal linear autoencoder
rows.operation_detail: Constructed optimal representations for generated datasets with different source supports; measured the angle of the most-mixed neuron's weight vector from its nearest source direction.
rows.measure: Angle-based proxy for modularity; the paper describes the resulting representation as mixed-selective.
rows.value: Removing a single critical datapoint changes the representation from modular to mixed-selective.
rows.note: The paper says its inequalities predict which generated datasets are modular and that the degree to which they are broken tracks the degree of mixing.

rows.subject: biologically constrained nonlinear feedforward network (What-Where Regression)
rows.operation_detail: Trained the network under biological constraints on what and where source variables, then measured conditional information-theoretic modularity.
rows.value: The hidden layer modularises what from where.
rows.note: This is a comparison condition in the study's range-support experiments; the report does not describe mixed-selective units for this setting.

rows.subject: biologically constrained nonlinear feedforward network (What-Where Regression)
rows.operation_detail: Trained the network on source distributions with progressively cut corners and measured representation modularity.

conditions.value: corner cutting; progressively more of the source-support corners removed

rows.value: Corner cutting increasingly degrades modularity and produces mixed-selective neurons.
rows.uncertainty: standard error of the mean shown in Figure 2
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative trend in the text; numerical plot values are not stated there.

rows.subject: biologically constrained nonlinear feedforward network (What-Where Regression)
rows.operation_detail: Trained on source distributions with correlations or diagonal removal that preserve the rectangular support boundary.

conditions.value: correlations introduced while preserving rectangular support, or diagonal data removed

rows.value: These changes affect modularity less than corner cutting; removing the diagonal does not induce mixing in the described extreme case.
rows.uncertainty: standard error of the mean shown in Figure 2
rows.note: The text compares these settings with corner cutting and describes the effect as smaller.
rows.check: The row merges two conditions. Range-preserving correlations still introduce some mixing ('introduces less mixing'), which is partial. Diagonal removal 'does not induce mixing', which is absent. Consider splitting the row.

source_check.correct: Separate the conditions: range-preserving correlations introduce less mixing than matched corner cutting, supporting partial; diagonal removal does not induce mixing, supporting absent.
source_check.problem: The combined row assigns partial to conditions with different stated outcomes.

rows.subject: linear RNN trained to report displacement to three objects
rows.operation_detail: Measured linear NCMI between neural activity and object outputs, then repeated the analysis as if the third object were unknown.

conditions.value: only the first and second objects are treated as known; the third is omitted

rows.measure: Linear NCMI of neural activity with the known object outputs
rows.baseline: analysis conditioning on all three objects
rows.value: Neurons that encode the omitted third object appear informative about the first and second objects and thus appear mixed-selective.
rows.note: The paper explains that conditioning on the omitted source is unavailable to the hypothetical experimenter; this is an apparent mixed-selectivity result caused by the analysis omitting a correlated variable.
rows.check: The neurons are actually modular. Mixed selectivity only appears because the analysis omits a correlated encoded variable. This is apparent, not real, polysemanticity, and bears on V3 only as a measurement caveat.

source_check.correct: For actual polysemanticity arising through an alternative mechanism, state=cannot_determine and version link=none. The neurons remain modular; omitting the third correlated object produces apparent mixed selectivity.

relationships.condition: Biologically constrained (nonnegative, energy-regularised) linear and nonlinear feedforward and recurrent networks with more units than sources, trained on range-dependent sources (corner cutting, harmonic frequencies, fixed reward locations)
relationships.reason: Mixed-selective neurons appear with no capacity shortage, driven by source range (r1, r3, r5, r7, r8, r10, r12, r14). Range-independent controls stay modular or mix less (r2, r4, r6, r9, r11, r13, r15), showing the mixing tracks the range manipulation.
relationships.display_finding: Neurons became mixed-selective even with more units than sources, driven by the range dependence of the sources. Range-independent controls stayed modular or mixed less, so the mixing tracked the range manipulation.
